patch_description: The current program's weakest metrics are smoothness (0.11) and slope_changes (162.8), while noise_reduction is already good (0.57) thanks to the robust Huber quadratic. Gen 3 showed that an adaptive constant-velocity Kalman pre-filter dramatically reduces slope changes (41.2) and boosts smoothness (0.33), because the Kalman state models slope and collapses its process noise when innovations are noise-consistent — noise can no longer flip the estimated trend. The edit: (1) insert an innovation-adaptive constant-velocity Kalman filter as a pre-smoothing stage over the raw signal, feeding its output into the existing robust weighted quadratic window fit; (2) use a MAD-based residual scale in the Huber pass instead of std (std is corrupted by the very outliers we want to suppress); (3) widen the post-smoothing kernel to a 5-tap binomial pass with edge-preserving handling to further cut spurious reversals without meaningful phase delay. This hybrid exploits the Kalman's noise-adaptive smoothing and the quadratic fit's zero-lag extrapolation, targeting slope_changes, false_reversals, and smoothness while preserving the lag and accuracy gains.
